text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- The government is prepared for negotiations. The Social Democrats take their time. Labour Minister Norbert Bluem says compromise is only possible if the SPD agree to save
- Teachers in the central state of Hesse have to work longer hours. In Baden-Wuerttemberg 1,600 new teachers jobs are needed
- Row over the state of the jobs market. A government spokesman says the 130,000 drop in unemployment was a good signal. but the SPD accused the government of failing to do anything about joblessness
- Doctors get access to virtual windowns. Practice information will soon be permitted on the Internet
- Several employees from the DGB German trade union federation protested against possible job losses
- Majority of German regional states reject Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition plans to reform the tax system -- because most are SPD-ruled
HANDELSBLATT

- Credit institutions must settle on the same day as a transfer is made, according to the Federal Court of Justice. Ruling came after complaints about a branch of Volksbank that transfered money the following day
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem offers opposition Social Democrats chance for talks about pension reform

- Still no change in trend in the jobs market. The economy cannot revive the jobs market. Despite a reduction of 130,000 in unemployment figures, joblessness in Germany remained at 4.347 million -- still a record high
- Hoechst management comes in for criticism from shareholders for failing to keep to company results forecasts
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Federal Court of Justice stops banks from making gains by delaying transactions. Transfers must be settled immediately, it ruled
- Number of unemployed has only dropped slightly. Economy remains weak
- The premier of Saxony state Kurt Biedenkopf criticised Chancellor Helmut Kohl for announcing his intention to run for a fourth term in 1998 general elections as "too early"
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl urges banks and industry to provide more venture capital
- The east German economy has stopped catching up with western Germany, according to Landeszentralbank
- Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt wants to strenthen the service sector
DIE WELT
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem offers a chance for the opposition Social Democrats to talk about pensions. SPD presidium decides on Monday

- Interior ministers from German regional states cancel their plans to accompany Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on a trip to Bosnia to try to coordinate better the return of refugees. Kinkel accuses them of holding up the refugees' return
- Bernhard Jagoda, President of the German Labour Office, needs additional billions of marks. Unemployment is making holes in his budget
- Bonn is opposed to salary privileges for EU officials
- Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt is hoping for a service industry boom, he announces an action programme for services
